meta.audience: The multitude gathered at Nephi's garden
meta.location: The garden of Nephi, by the highway to the chief market in Zarahemla
principles: A prophet rejected in one land and heard in another
A warning that names its own source

world_behind.title: He comes home from a failed mission
world_behind.text: Verses 1 to 3 have him preaching in the land northward, rejected entirely, and returning to the land of his nativity. Helaman 3:3 to 12 records the migration that filled the north with Nephites inside his own father's lifetime, so the ground he was working was recently settled.

world_behind.title: The robbers already held the government
world_behind.text: Helaman 6:38 and 39 report the Nephites building the band up until it obtained the sole management of the government and trampled the poor. Verses 4 and 5 describe what that looked like from the street: the righteous condemned, the guilty acquitted for money.

world_behind.title: The sixty-ninth year is late in the decline
world_behind.text: Verse 1 gives the date. Helaman 6:15 had the chief judge Cezoram and his son both murdered in the sixty-sixth. Three years separate a government losing two heads and a prophet praying on a tower about it.

world_behind.title: The tower stands on the road to the market
world_behind.text: Verse 10 puts it in his own garden, beside the garden gate, on the highway that led to the chief market in Zarahemla. No other private garden in the record is placed this carefully, and it is placed because the location is what gathered the crowd.

world_behind.title: The comparison with the Lamanites is not new
world_behind.text: Helaman 6:1 had already said Lamanite righteousness exceeded Nephite because of their firmness and steadiness in the faith. Verses 23 and 24 repeat the judgment and supply the reason: they have not sinned against the same knowledge.

world_behind.title: What he claims here is tested two chapters later
world_behind.text: Verse 29 says he does not speak these things of himself. Helaman 8:27 has him name a murder nobody present knew of, and Helaman 9:3 has five men run to the judgment-seat and find it exactly so.

words.text: Treated at Alma 21:1, of Aaron leaving his own land. The record uses the word twice. Verse 3 uses it of the place a rejected preacher goes back to.

Persuaded, prevailed upon by asking. The record uses the word twice, here and at Alma 7:23. Verse 7 lists it first among the qualities of the first generation, ahead of firmness, slowness to sin, and quickness to hearken.
Treated at Alma 9:11, of a people handed over to a state. Nephi applies it to himself and to the era he was born into, in a sentence he cannot argue his way out of.
A place of public buying and selling. The word occurs once in the record and seven times in the King James Bible. It fixes the tower's location on the busiest road in the city.
To throw with force. It appears once in the record, and three times in the King James Bible. Verse 16 has the devil hurling souls down to misery, in a sentence about how they gave way to him.
To extend in time. The record uses the word six times, including Lehi's account of the days granted to men in 2 Nephi 2:21. Verse 24 promises lengthened days and increased seed to the Lamanites.

phrases.term: They did reject all his words, insomuch that he could not stay among them
phrases.text: The record reports a mission with no converts. Nephi leaves because staying is no longer possible.

phrases.term: Those Gadianton robbers filling the judgment-seats
phrases.text: Helaman 6:39 had them obtaining the government. This verse shows what that looks like from the street.

phrases.term: Letting the guilty and the wicked go unpunished because of their money
phrases.text: The charge stated as a transaction. The same verse has the righteous condemned for their righteousness, so the courts run in both directions.

phrases.term: Oh, that I could have had my days in the days when my father Nephi first came out of the land of Jerusalem
phrases.text: A prophet wishing he had lived six hundred years earlier. He names what he would have wanted: joy in the righteousness of his brethren.

phrases.term: I am consigned that these are my days
phrases.text: The wish closed off in one sentence. He accepts the era and the sorrow that comes with it, and then climbs the tower.

phrases.term: A tower, which was in the garden of Nephi, which was by the highway which led to the chief market
phrases.text: The most carefully located spot in the book. Mormon gives garden, tower, gate, and highway, which is why anyone saw him at all.

phrases.term: Why have ye gathered yourselves together? That I may tell you of your iniquities?
phrases.text: Nephi opens by asking what they came for. The question puts the burden of the meeting on the crowd.

phrases.term: Ye are given away that the devil has got so great hold upon your hearts
phrases.text: His answer to their marveling. They marvel at his grief, and he says the thing worth marveling at is their own condition.

phrases.term: Ye will not hearken unto the voice of the good shepherd
phrases.text: The reason given for God's withdrawal. Alma 5:38 had made hearing that voice the test of whose sheep a person is.

phrases.term: It shall be better for the Lamanites than for you except ye shall repent
phrases.text: The comparison Helaman 6:1 had already established as fact. Verse 24 gives the reason as knowledge received and sinned against.

phrases.term: I do not say that these things shall be, of myself
phrases.text: The chapter's last move. Nephi separates his own judgment from what he was told, and testifies only to the second.

verses.label: v. 2–3
verses.title: A complete failure reported without consolation
verses.text: The record gives the mission and its outcome in two sentences and adds nothing to soften it: he "did preach the word of God unto them, and did prophesy many things unto them," and "they did reject all his words, insomuch that he could not stay among them, but returned again unto the land of his nativity." No converts are counted, no remnant is named, and no reason is offered beyond the rejection itself. The chapter's whole starting position is a prophet who has just been run out of a country.

verses.label: v. 13–15
verses.title: The sermon opens by explaining the audience to itself
verses.text: The first thing said from the tower is a question about why the hearers are there, and the answer is not flattering to them: "why have ye gathered yourselves together? That I may tell you of your iniquities? Yea, because I have got upon my tower that I might pour out my soul unto my God, because of the exceeding sorrow of my heart." Verse 15 turns their curiosity into the charge: "ye have gathered yourselves together, and do marvel; yea, and ye have great need to marvel." They came to watch a man weep and are told that the weeping is about them.

verses.label: v. 29
verses.title: A disclaimer placed at the end rather than the beginning
verses.text: After twenty-eight verses of accusation and prediction, the record has the speaker separate his authority from his person: "I do not say that these things shall be, of myself, because it is not of myself that I know these things; but behold, I know that these things are true because the Lord God has made them known unto me." I do not say stands in five verses of the volume, three of them in Alma 40 and one at Alma 7:8. Each time it marks the edge of what the speaker will claim on his own account.

chapter.title: The sermon begins with a failed mission
chapter.text: Verses 1 through 3 establish that Nephi has just been refused a hearing elsewhere. The crowd in Zarahemla assembles for a reason he did not arrange.

chapter.title: Grief is what gathers them
chapter.text: Verse 10 spends its whole length on position, nesting four locations: "upon a tower, which was in the garden of Nephi, which was by the highway which led to the chief market, which was in the city of Zarahemla." Verse 11 supplies the mechanism, passers-by who "ran and told the people what they had seen," and the crowd assembles for that reason. Verse 13 has the speaker ask them why they came, "Behold, why have ye gathered yourselves together?" No sermon was announced; the record gives a garden, a road, and a market as the cause.

chapter.title: Nephi asks before he tells
chapter.text: Verse 13 puts a question to the crowd about their own motive. The sermon starts as an interrogation of why they showed up.

chapter.title: The lament is honest and closed
chapter.text: Verses 7 and 8 wish for another century, and verse 9 stops wishing. The record lets a prophet want a different assignment and then take this one.

chapter.title: Justice for sale is the specific charge
chapter.text: Verse 5 names money as the mechanism. The political collapse of Helaman 6 is reported here as courtroom practice.

chapter.title: The Lamanite comparison turns on knowledge
chapter.text: Verse 24 says they have not sinned against the great knowledge the Nephites received. The measure is what a people was given, not what they achieved.

chapter.title: Scattering replaces gathering
chapter.text: Verse 19 sets the two against each other as the alternative outcomes. The promise of the land runs both ways.

chapter.title: The last verse is about authority
chapter.text: Nephi disclaims his own knowledge before affirming the prophecy. Helaman 8 opens with judges attacking him, and this verse is already positioned for it.

applications.title: Go home and keep working
applications.text: Rejected in the north, Nephi returned and started again in Zarahemla. A closed door is information about that place, not about the work.

applications.title: Watch what money does to the verdicts
applications.text: Nephi's charge is that the guilty went unpunished because of their money while the righteous were condemned for their righteousness. To test whether a system is sound, look at who gets away with things and ask what those people have in common.

applications.title: Stop wishing at some point
applications.text: He wanted another century and then accepted this one in a single line. Naming the wish and closing it is what lets the next verse happen.

applications.title: Know what your position makes visible
applications.text: Nephi's tower stood in his garden beside the highway that ran to the chief market. He was not performing, and the location still did work he had not planned on.

applications.title: Let people see you care
applications.text: A crowd formed because a man's grief was visible from the road. Sincere feeling, plainly shown, gathers attention that argument does not.

applications.title: Ask what they came for
applications.text: Nephi opened with a question about their motives. Knowing why someone is listening changes what is worth saying.

applications.title: Notice how quickly the forgetting happens
applications.text: Nephi asks how they could have forgotten God in the very day that he delivered them. Gratitude has a short half-life, so put the remembering on a schedule instead of trusting it to arrive.

applications.title: Say where you got it
applications.text: Nephi ends by disclaiming his own authorship of the prophecy and naming its source. When you deliver hard news on somebody else's authority, be exact about whose, since that is the part your hearer has to weigh.

questions.text: Where have I kept pushing at a door that is shut?
Where have I seen a rule bend for money and said nothing?
What earlier time do I wish I had lived in, and why?
What am I consigned to that I have not yet accepted?
What would someone passing by learn about what I care about?
What did I forget about God on the very day something went right?
When I say something will happen, do I know how I know?
